facts.quote: It has an area of 30,000 square metres (320,000 sq ft) and is 158 metres (518 ft) tall. However, it also includes a rectory and a villa (counted in the overall area), which are not strictly part of the church. It can accommodate 18,000 worshippers, compared to 60,000 for St. Peter's.

facts.fact: It was built between 1985 and 1989; its dome and encircled plaza were inspired by St Peter's in Rome, though it is not a replica.
facts.quote: The basilica was constructed between 1985 and 1989 with different cost estimates given by various groups. Some stated that it cost US$175 million, US$300 million, or as high as US$600 million. The designs of the dome and encircled plaza were inspired by the Basilica of Saint Peter in Vatican City, although it is not an outright replica.

facts.fact: Architect Pierre Fakhoury made the dome slightly lower than St Peter's but topped it with a larger cross.
facts.quote: While designing it after the Vatican basilica, the Lebanese architect Pierre Fakhoury constructed the dome to be slightly lower than the Basilica of Saint Peter, but topped with a larger cross.

facts.fact: The dome is 90 m across, more than twice St Peter's 41 m.
facts.quote: The dome is more than twice the diameter of St. Peter's in Rome, 90 metres (300 ft) versus 41 metres (135 ft).

facts.fact: It is built of Italian marble with 8,400 m² of contemporary French stained glass.
facts.quote: The basilica is constructed with marble imported from Italy and is furnished with 8,400 square metres (90,000 sq ft) of contemporary stained glass from France.

facts.fact: The smaller columns are structural; the larger ones are decorative and hide lifts, rainwater pipes and other services.
facts.quote: Columns are plentiful throughout the basilica but are not uniform in style; the smaller columns are structural, while the larger ones are decorative and contain elevators, rainwater conduits from the roof and other building mechanical devices.

facts.fact: Pope John Paul II consecrated it on 10 September 1990.
facts.quote: The cornerstone was laid on 10 August 1985, and it was consecrated on 10 September 1990 by Pope John Paul II, who had just formally accepted the basilica as a gift from  Félix Houphouët-Boigny on behalf of the Catholic Church.

facts.fact: The Atatürk Library (1973) is named among the important Turkish designs of the 1970s.
facts.quote: Some important designs from the 1970s are the Turkish Language Association Building (1972), Atatürk Library (1973) and Abdi İpekçi Arena (1979).

facts.fact: The Darat al-Funun Art Center in Amman is one of Ammar Khammash's important projects.
facts.quote: Darat al-Funun Art Center, Amman

facts.fact: Khammash's work integrates buildings with nature and their surroundings.
facts.quote: His work is based on the integration of building designs with nature and the surrounding environment.

facts.fact: It is a public library in Sant Martí de Provençals, Barcelona, inaugurated on 28 May 2022.
facts.quote: The Biblioteca Gabriel García Márquez is a public library located in Sant Martí de Provençals, a neighborhood of Barcelona. It was inaugurated on 28 May 2022.

facts.fact: It specialises in Latin American literature and is named after Gabriel García Márquez, who lived in Barcelona from 1967 to 1975.
facts.quote: It specializes in Latin American literature and is named after the Colombian writer Gabriel García Márquez, who lived in the Catalan capital between 1967 and 1975, where he wrote The Autumn of the Patriarch (El otoño del patriarca).

facts.fact: It was designed by SUMA Arquitectura, led by Elena Orte and Guillermo Sevillano.
facts.quote: The building was designed by Suma Arquitectura, a studio led by architects Elena Orte and Guillermo Sevillano.

facts.fact: With six floors and about 4,000 m², it is Barcelona's third-largest library.
facts.quote: The building has six floors and with about 4,000 m2 of floor it is the third largest library in Barcelona.

facts.fact: Wood is used throughout, for a welcoming feel and a smaller environmental footprint.
facts.quote: The use of wood throughout the building stands out, a material that provides a welcoming atmosphere and contributes to the aim of reducing the centre's environmental footprint.

facts.fact: From outside it looks like a stack of open books.
facts.quote: Its appearance from the outside resembles a stack of open books.

facts.fact: In August 2023 IFLA named it the best new public library in the world.
facts.quote: In August 2023 the library was declared the "best new public library in the world" by the International Federation of Library Associations and Institutions.

facts.fact: CINiBA is a joint scientific library of the University of Silesia and the University of Economics in Katowice, at the heart of the campus.
facts.quote: The Scientific Information Center and Academic Library  (CINiBA) is a joint scientific library of two universities in Katowice - the University of Silesia in Katowice and the University of Economics in Katowice.  It is located in the heart of the university campus, in the center of the Silesian agglomeration.

facts.fact: Its design came from a two-stage SARP competition, completed in March 2003 and won by architects from Koszalin and Radom.
facts.quote: March 24, 2003 — the two-stage competition of the Association of Polish Architects (SARP) for the creation of the concept of the Scientific Information Center and the Academic Library of the University of Silesia was completed. The winner was a team of architects from Koszalin and Radom.

facts.fact: It opened to readers on 27 September 2012.
facts.quote: September 27, 2012 — opening of the library for readers.

facts.fact: The building has 7 floors and 4,004 windows.
facts.quote: Building: 7 floors, 4004 windows

facts.fact: Up to 1,000 people can be in the building at the same time.
facts.quote: 1000 people can stay in the building at the same time

facts.fact: Most materials are on open shelves that users can reach freely.
facts.quote: Being a joint project of the University of Silesia and University of Economics in Katowice, most of the materials are available in the open space to which users have free access.

facts.fact: The Petroperú Building in San Isidro, Lima, is the head office of the state oil company Petroperú.
facts.quote: The Petroperú Building is a building located in San Isidro District, Lima. It functions as the main office of Petroperú, a state company dedicated to refining, transporting, distributing and marketing oil in Peru.

facts.fact: Designed by Daniel Arana Ríos and Walter Weberhofer, it won a contest held by Juan Velasco Alvarado's military government in the early 1970s.
facts.quote: The building, designed by the architects Daniel Arana Ríos and Walter Weberhofer, was the winning design in a contest organised by the military government of Juan Velasco Alvarado in the early 1970s.

facts.fact: It was inaugurated in 1973.
facts.quote: The building, strategically located in central San Isidro, was projected to host the offices of state company Petroperú, being inaugurated in 1973.

facts.fact: It has 22 floors, three basements and a rooftop helipad, and is Brutalist in style.
facts.quote: It has twenty-two floors and three basements in addition to having a helipad on top and is part of the architectural style known as brutalism.

facts.fact: It also houses the Ministry of Housing, other public offices and art galleries.
facts.quote: In addition to Petroperú, the building houses several public offices as well as the Ministry of Housing, Construction and Sanitation, the Agency for the Promotion of Private Investment and several art galleries.

facts.fact: Weberhofer's list of works dates it 1969–1973.
facts.quote: Edificio Petroperú (1969–1973, with Daniel Arana Ríos)

facts.fact: The City of Justice stands on Gran Via in Barcelona's Sants-Montjuïc and neighbouring L'Hospitalet de Llobregat.
facts.quote: The Ciutat de la Justícia de Barcelona i l'Hospitalet de Llobregat or just Ciutat de la Justícia (Catalan for City of Justice) is a recent architectural development in the Sants-Montjuïc district of Barcelona and its immediately adjacent suburb of l'Hospitalet de Llobregat, on Gran Via de les Corts Catalanes near Plaça d'Ildefons Cerdà and Plaça d'Europa.

facts.fact: It gathers legal departments that were previously spread over 17 buildings in both cities.
facts.quote: It hosts most of the legal departments of the metropolitan area, which were previously located in 17 separate buildings scattered around both cities.

facts.fact: It was part of the urban regeneration of L'Hospitalet in the 2000s and 2010s.
facts.quote: It was envisioned as part of the urban regeneration program for L'Hospitalet de Llobregat that has taken place over the decades of the 2000s and 2010s.

facts.fact: Courtrooms are on the ground floor with offices above, and four buildings are linked by a four-storey hall.
facts.quote: The courtrooms are on the ground floor, with offices above. Four of the buildings are connected together by a four-storey hallway.

facts.fact: The complex also includes a commercial centre, shops and a block of low-income housing.
facts.quote: In addition to the judicial buildings, the complex, on the outskirts of Barcelona, includes a commercial centre and retail stores, and a block of low income residential housing.

facts.fact: All façades are cast-in-place concrete, lightly tinted in different shades.
facts.quote: The facades of the buildings are all the same, made of concrete poured in place and lightly tinted in different shades.

facts.fact: Chipperfield aimed to 'break the image of justice as rigid and monolithic'; The Guardian's Rowan Moore found it 'uncomfortably prison-like'.
facts.quote: Chipperfield wrote that the purpose of the building was to "break the image of justice as rigid and monolithic", but architectural critic Rowan Moore of The Guardian said it appeared "uncomfortably prison-like."

facts.fact: Aviva Stadium in Dublin seats 51,711 and stands on the site of the old Lansdowne Road Stadium, demolished in 2007.
facts.quote: It has a capacity of 51,711 (all seated). It is built on the site of the former Lansdowne Road Stadium, which was demolished in 2007, and replaced it as home to its chief tenants: the Ireland national rugby union team and the Republic of Ireland football team.

facts.fact: It opened on 14 May 2010 beside Lansdowne Road railway station.
facts.quote: The stadium, located beside Lansdowne Road railway station, officially opened on 14 May 2010.

facts.fact: It was designed by Populous with Scott Tallon Walker Architects.
facts.quote: The Aviva Stadium in Dublin, Ireland, on the site of the old Lansdowne Road site, was designed by Populous in collaboration with Scott Tallon Walker Architects.

facts.fact: Designed as a sweeping crystalline bowl, it harvests rainwater for the pitch, reuses waste heat for hot water and has a transparent roof that lets in daylight.
facts.quote: Designed as a sweeping crystalline bowl, the stadium harvests rainwater to irrigate the field, reuses waste heat for hot water, and is topped with a transparent roof that allows daylight to suffuse the interior spaces.

facts.fact: It was Ireland's first UEFA Category 4 stadium.
facts.quote: The stadium was Ireland's first UEFA Category 4 Stadium, and hosted the 2011 and the 2024 UEFA Europa League finals.

facts.fact: It won a British Construction Industry Award in 2011.
facts.quote: In 2011, the stadium won a British Construction Industry Award.

facts.fact: Dunelm House is a Grade II listed Brutalist building in Durham, built in 1966, housing Durham Students' Union.
facts.quote: Dunelm House is a Grade II listed building in Durham, England, built in 1966 in the brutalist style. It belongs to Durham University and houses Durham Students' Union.

facts.fact: Its listing calls it a significant Brutalist building and 'the foremost students' union building of the post-war era in England'.
facts.quote: Its listing entry cites, among other factors, that it is "a significant Brutalist building that reflects the latest in architectural thinking for its date" and that it is "the foremost students’ union building of the post-war era in England".

facts.fact: It was designed by Richard Raines and Michael Powers of the Architects' Co-Partnership, with engineer Ove Arup, whose Kingsgate Bridge stands next to it.
facts.quote: The brutalist angular concrete building was designed by Richard Raines and Michael Powers of the Architects' Co-Partnership, and completed in 1966 under the supervision of engineer Sir Ove Arup, whose adjacent Kingsgate Bridge opened two years earlier.

facts.fact: Built into the steep bank of the River Wear, it has a straight main staircase through all five levels, meant to feel like an interior street.
facts.quote: Built into the steeply sloping bank of the River Wear, Dunelm House is notable internally for the fact that the main staircase linking all five levels of the building runs in an entirely straight line. This was intended by the building's architects to create the feeling of an interior street.

facts.fact: Its levels cascade down the river bank, echoing the city's vernacular and breaking up its bulk.
facts.quote: It has also been recognised for the way its multiple levels cascade down the river bank, reflecting the vernacular architecture of the city and breaking up the bulk of the building.

facts.fact: It won a Civic Trust award in 1968; Pevsner called it 'Brutalist by tradition but not brutal to the landscape'.
facts.quote: In 1968 Dunelm House won a Civic Trust award. Sir Nikolaus Pevsner, the noted architecture historian, considered the building, "Brutalist by tradition but not brutal to the landscape ... the elements, though bold, [are] sensitively composed."

facts.fact: After the university planned demolition in 2016, appeals by the Twentieth Century Society led to Grade II listing, announced in 2021.
facts.quote: The initial appeal was unsuccessful but a second appeal on the grounds that there were irregularities in the listing process and evidence that the decision had been wrongly made led to an announcement in 2021 that the building would be listed at Grade II.

facts.fact: The Boston Government Service Center is a state government complex in Boston's West End, designed in the Brutalist style and led by Paul Rudolph.
facts.quote: The Boston Government Service Center (BGSC) is a state government complex in the West End of Boston, Massachusetts. The center was designed in the Brutalist style, led by architect Paul Rudolph.

facts.fact: Two large, connected buildings snake around a plaza, with three corners squared off to make small street-side plazas.
facts.quote: On the site are two large buildings, structurally separate yet connected, that snake around a plaza, aligned with the street except with three corners squared off, creating three small streetside plazas around the building.

facts.fact: Desmond & Lord designed the Lindemann Building with Rudolph, and Shepley Bulfinch Richardson and Abbott designed the Hurley Building.
facts.quote: Desmond & Lord designed the Lindemann Building with Rudolph, and Shepley Bulfinch Richardson and Abbott designed the Hurley Building.

facts.fact: It was designed in contrast to the nearby City Hall and inspired by the idea of an amphitheatre where citizens could watch civic dramas unfold.
facts.quote: The structure was designed in contrast to the City Hall a few blocks away, and was inspired by the idea of an amphitheater that would allow citizens to experience civic dramas unfolding.

facts.fact: Inside and out it uses ribbed, bush-hammered 'corduroy' concrete, a finish Rudolph developed in his earlier Yale Art and Architecture Building.
facts.quote: The interior and exterior of the building utilize ribbed, bush-hammered concrete (also known as "corduroy concrete"), a form Rudolph developed in his earlier Yale Art and Architecture Building.

facts.fact: Tall columns at regular intervals hold lifts, stairs and bathrooms, and stepped terraces and concrete sunshades surround the central plaza.
facts.quote: Other representative elements include its several-story-high columns, placed regularly, which contain elevators, staircases, and bathrooms; and the buildings' stepped terraces and concrete sunshades surrounding the central plaza.

facts.fact: Construction ran from 1966 into 1971, and funding cuts in 1970 cancelled the planned tower and the swirling terraces at its base.
facts.quote: Construction began in 1966 and lasted into 1971. Most of the complex was completed in that year, including most of the serpentine structure, interior courtyard, and plaza. Funding cuts in 1970 led to the cancellation of the tower and swirling terraces at its base.

facts.fact: The Boston Landmarks Commission reported in 1990 that the complex is eligible for the National Register of Historic Places, though it is not currently listed as a landmark.
facts.quote: While the Government Service Center is not currently listed as a national, state, or local landmark, the Boston Landmarks Commission reported in 1990 that the complex is eligible for the National Register of Historic Places, and its exterior and select interiors as a Boston Landmark.

facts.fact: The Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall is a national monument in Taipei built in memory of Chiang Kai-shek, former President of the Republic of China.
facts.quote: The Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall (Chinese: 中正紀念堂; pinyin: zhōngzhèng jìniàntáng; Pe̍h-ōe-jī: Tiong-chèng-kí-liām-tn̂g) is a national monument and tourist attraction erected during Taiwan’s martial law period in memory of Chiang Kai-shek, former President of the Republic of China.

facts.fact: It stands at the east end of Memorial Hall Square, flanked by the National Theater and the National Concert Hall.
facts.quote: The monument, surrounded by a park, stands at the east end of Memorial Hall Square. It is flanked on the north and south by the National Theater and National Concert Hall.

facts.fact: Its blue octagonal roof draws on the number eight, linked in Chinese culture with abundance and good fortune.
facts.quote: The roof is blue and octagonal, a shape that picks up the symbolism of the number eight, a number traditionally associated in Chinese culture with abundance and good fortune.

facts.fact: Two sets of white stairs, each with 89 steps for Chiang's age at his death, lead to the main entrance.
facts.quote: Two sets of white stairs, each with 89 steps to represent Chiang's age at the time of his death, lead to the main entrance.

facts.fact: Architect Yang Cho-cheng's design was chosen in a competition.
facts.quote: The design, by architect Yang Cho-cheng, was chosen in a competition.

facts.fact: Yang's design used many elements of traditional Chinese architecture to mirror the Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum in Nanjing.
facts.quote: Yang's design incorporated many elements of traditional Chinese architecture to mirror that of the Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum in Nanjing, China.

facts.fact: The hall officially opened on 5 April 1980, the fifth anniversary of Chiang's death.
facts.quote: The hall officially opened on April 5, 1980, the fifth anniversary of the leader's death.

facts.fact: The square became Taipei's main place for mass gatherings and the hub of events that brought Taiwan into modern democracy.
facts.quote: The square became Taipei's site of choice for mass gatherings as soon as it opened. The nature of many of those gatherings gave the site new public meanings. The hall and square became the hub of events in the 1980s and early 1990s that ushered Taiwan into its era of modern democracy.

facts.fact: Hong Kong Design Institute is a public design school in Tiu Keng Leng, Tseung Kwan O, Hong Kong.
facts.quote: Hong Kong Design Institute (HKDI) is a public design school in Tiu Keng Leng, Tseung Kwan O, Hong Kong.

facts.fact: It was founded in 2007 and moved into a purpose-built campus in 2010.
facts.quote: It was founded by the Vocational Training Council in 2007 and moved into a purpose-built campus in 2010.

facts.fact: In April 2006 an international architecture competition was opened to design a new campus for 4,000 students.
facts.quote: In April 2006, the VTC opened an international architecture competition to design a new campus able to accommodate 4,000 students.

facts.fact: The jury included architects Richard Meier and Rocco Yim.
facts.quote: The competition was judged by a panel of noted architects including Richard Meier and Rocco Yim.

facts.fact: The French firm Coldefy & Associés won, beating 162 other entries.
facts.quote: The winning design, which beat out 162 other submissions, was produced by the French architecture firm Coldefy & Associés.

facts.fact: A massive rectangular volume is suspended seven storeys above the street on four towers supported by a steel lattice exoskeleton.
facts.quote: The building comprises a massive rectangular volume suspended seven storeys above street level on four towers supported by a steel lattice exoskeleton.

facts.fact: The podium holds four auditoriums and lecture theatres, a cafe, and gallery and exhibition space.
facts.quote: The podium houses four auditoriums and lecture theaters, a cafe, and gallery and exhibition space.

facts.fact: Footbridges link it to the neighbouring IVE Lee Wai Lee campus.
facts.quote: The two buildings are linked together by footbridges.

facts.fact: The Casa Sindical is a building in Madrid that now houses Spain's Ministry of Health.
facts.quote: The Casa Sindical (the "Syndical House") is a building in Madrid, Spain. It currently hosts the headquarters of the Ministry of Health of Spain.

facts.fact: The project was awarded jointly to Francisco de Asís Cabrero and Rafael de Aburto after a competition announced in 1949.
facts.quote: The project was finally entrusted ex-aequo to Francisco de Asís Cabrero and Rafael de Aburto.

facts.fact: It was finished in 1951 and formally inaugurated by Francisco Franco on 27 October 1955.
facts.quote: Finished in 1951, some dependencies were opened in July 1955, taking advantage of the celebration of the III National Congress of Workers. It was formally inaugurated by Francisco Franco on 27 October 1955.

facts.fact: Facing the Prado Museum, it has a central prism-shaped brick tower of 16 floors, 60 metres high.
facts.quote: Located in front of the Prado Museum, it features a central prismatic 16-floor brick tower, that reaches a 60-metre height.

facts.fact: It marked the Franco regime's acceptance of modern architecture, moving away from traditionalist styles.
facts.quote: The landmark symbolically marked the acceptance of modern architecture by the Francoist regime in terms of architectural language, straying away from previous traditionalist aesthetics.

facts.fact: It has often been linked to the work of the Italian architect Giuseppe Terragni.
facts.quote: It has often been linked to the works of Italian Fascist architect Giuseppe Terragni.

facts.fact: The Casa Sindical is one of Rafael Aburto's best-known works.
facts.quote: His most famous works are Casa Sindical de Madrid and Obra Sindical del Hogar.

facts.fact: Denton Corker Marshall designed the Museum of Sydney.
facts.quote: Other projects by the practice include the multi-award-winning Manchester Civil Justice Centre, a new visitors' centre at Stonehenge, Sydney's Governor Phillip Tower, the Museum of Sydney, extensions to the Australian War Memorial and Australian embassies in Tokyo and Beijing.

facts.fact: The Colonnade Bridge crosses the Váh river in Piešťany, linking the town to the Spa Island.
facts.quote: Kolonádový most (literally The Colonnade Bridge) is a bridge over the Váh river in Piešťany. It connects the town to the Spa Island.

facts.fact: Emil Belluš designed it in 1930–33 in Streamline Moderne, a style of Art Deco from the 1930s.
facts.quote: The bridge was designed by architect Emil Belluš in 1930–33, in Streamline Moderne, an international style of Art Deco architecture that emerged in the 1930s.

facts.fact: The middle of the bridge has glass engravings by the artist Martin Benka.
facts.quote: The center of the bridge features glass engravings by a well-known artist Martin Benka titled "Detva Songs" and "At Sheepcote".

facts.fact: Its entrances carry Latin inscriptions, including the spa's motto 'Surge et ambula' (Get up and walk).
facts.quote: The western entrance of the bridge features an inscription in Classical Latin: "Saluberrimae Pistinienses Thermae" (The healing Piešťany Spa) and the eastern entrance features the spa's motto "Surge et ambula" (Get up and walk).

facts.fact: The 'Crutch Breaker' statue, symbol of the spa, by sculptor Robert Kuhmayer (1934), stands at the western entrance.
facts.quote: The "Crutch Breaker" statue and the symbol of the spa, stands at the western entrance. The sculpture is the work of the Academic Sculptor Robert Kuhmayer (created in 1934).

facts.fact: The retreating German army destroyed the bridge in 1945; rebuilt, it reopened on 30 December 1956.
facts.quote: The bridge was destroyed in 1945 by the retreating German army; after reconstruction it was re-opened on 30 December 1956.

facts.fact: Belluš worked in an international functionalist style but was willing to add classical elements, as at this bridge.
facts.quote: While working in an international functionalist style, he was willing to modify it with classical elements, as can be seen in the Colonnade Bridge at Piešťany completed in 1932.

facts.fact: Stadio Renato Dall'Ara is a multi-purpose stadium in Bologna, home of Bologna FC.
facts.quote: Stadio Renato Dall'Ara is a multi-purpose stadium in Bologna, Italy. It is currently used mostly for football matches and the home of Bologna FC.

facts.fact: Giulio Ulisse Arata designed it, and it opened in 1927 as the Stadio Littoriale.
facts.quote: The stadium was designed by Giulio Ulisse Arata and inaugurated in 1927 as Stadio Littoriale.

facts.fact: It was one of the first stadiums to build the stands into the architecture, which later became a model worldwide.
facts.quote: It was one of the first stadiums to incorporate the stands into the architecture, an innovation which later became the model for stadiums around the world.

facts.fact: Its large arch held an equestrian statue of Mussolini, destroyed in 1943.
facts.quote: The large arch contained an equestrian statue of the dictator Benito Mussolini, which was destroyed during the city's liberation in 1943.

facts.fact: It hosted matches in the 1934 and 1990 FIFA World Cups, and the 1990 tournament required expansion and modernisation.
facts.quote: The stadium hosted matches in both the 1934 FIFA World Cup and the 1990 FIFA World Cup. Its inclusion in the latter demanded both expansion and modernisation.

facts.fact: For 1990 an exposed steel frame of 120 columns, lined up with the old pilasters, was added to carry the extended terrace and stairs.
facts.quote: To facilitate this, an exposed steel framework, incorporating 120 columns, was aligned with the pre-existing pilasters, supporting the extended terrace and providing access via a series of stairwells running around the stadium’s perimeter.

facts.fact: The stadium has around 36,000 seats, rising to 55,000 for concerts.
facts.quote: The stadium has around 36,000 seats and its capacity can be increased up to 55,000 for concerts.

facts.fact: Cambridge University Library is the main research library of the University of Cambridge.
facts.quote: Cambridge University Library is the main research library of the University of Cambridge.

facts.fact: It is one of six legal deposit libraries under UK law.
facts.quote: Cambridge University Library is one of six legal deposit libraries under UK law.

facts.fact: The building, designed by Giles Gilbert Scott, opened in 1934.
facts.quote: The current building, designed by Giles Gilbert Scott, opened in 1934.

facts.fact: It was built between 1931 and 1934 and is Grade II listed.
facts.quote: It was constructed between 1931 and 1934. It is a Grade II listed building.

facts.fact: John D. Rockefeller funded most of the building and persuaded the architect to add the front-facing tower for a grander entrance.
facts.quote: The American philanthropist John D. Rockefeller provided the largest part of the funds for the library's construction. Sensing that it needed a grander entrance, Rockefeller persuaded the architect to add the distinctive front-facing tower.

facts.fact: The building resembles Scott's industrial architecture, including Bankside Power Station, now Tate Modern.
facts.quote: The building bears a resemblance to Scott's industrial architecture, including Bankside Power Station (now Tate Modern).

facts.fact: The tower is 157 feet (48 m) tall.
facts.quote: The library tower stands 157 feet (48 m) tall, 6 feet (1.8 m) shorter than the top of St John's College Chapel and 10 feet (3.0 m) taller than the peak of King's College Chapel.

facts.fact: The library has been extended several times with ground-level and underground additions.
facts.quote: The library has been extended several times through ground annexes and underground extensions which allowed for new legal deposit documents to be stored.

facts.fact: Galway Cathedral is a Roman Catholic cathedral, built from 1958 on the site of the old Galway Gaol.
facts.quote: The Cathedral of Our Lady Assumed into Heaven and St Nicholas (Irish language: Ard-Eaglais Mhaighdean na Deastógála agus Naomh Nioclás), commonly known as Galway Cathedral, is a Roman Catholic cathedral in Galway, Ireland. Construction began in 1958 on the site of the old Galway Gaol.

facts.fact: Completed in 1965, it has been called 'the last great stone cathedral to be built in Europe'.
facts.quote: It was completed in 1965, lending it the designation of being "the last great stone cathedral to be built in Europe".

facts.fact: Its dome and pillars reflect a Renaissance style, while the rose windows and mosaics follow the broad tradition of Christian art.
facts.quote: The dome and pillars reflect a Renaissance style. Other features, including the rose windows and mosaics, echo the broad tradition of Christian art.

facts.fact: The dome, 44.2 metres high, is a landmark on the city skyline.
facts.quote: The cathedral dome, at a height of 44.2 metres (145 ft), is a prominent landmark on the city skyline.

facts.fact: Built almost entirely of local limestone, it is considered the last stone public building in Ireland.
facts.quote: Constructed nearly entirely of local limestone, the cathedral is considered to be last stone public building in Ireland.

facts.fact: The client wanted a traditional style, although many thought a 1950s-style cathedral should be built.
facts.quote: Although many were of the opinion that a 1950s style cathedral should be built, the client wanted a traditional style building.

facts.fact: Architect John J. Robinson was hired in 1949 to design the cathedral.
facts.quote: In 1949, architect John J Robinson was hired to design the Galway Cathedral.

facts.fact: The Daily Express Building at 120 Fleet Street, London, is Grade II* listed.
facts.quote: The Daily Express Building (120 Fleet Street) is a Grade II* listed building located in Fleet Street in the City of London.

facts.fact: Ellis & Clarke designed it in 1932 as the home of the Daily Express, and it is one of London's most prominent Art Deco / Streamline Moderne buildings.
facts.quote: It was designed in 1932 by Ellis & Clarke to serve as the home of the Daily Express newspaper and is one of the most prominent examples of art-deco / Streamline Moderne architecture in London.

facts.fact: Its black façade with rounded corners is made of Vitrolite and clear glass with chromium strips.
facts.quote: The exterior features a black façade with rounded corners in vitrolite and clear glass, with chromium strips.

facts.fact: The lobby, by Robert Atkinson, has plaster reliefs by Eric Aumonier, silver and gilt decoration, a silvered pendant lamp and an oval staircase.
facts.quote: The flamboyant lobby, designed by Robert Atkinson, includes plaster reliefs by Eric Aumonier, silver and gilt decorations, a magnificent silvered pendant lamp and an oval staircase.

facts.fact: The listing also covers its massive reinforced concrete stacked portal frame structure, designed by Sir Owen Williams.
facts.quote: The Grade II* listing relates not only to the architectural features but also to the massive reinforced concrete stacked portal frame structure designed by Sir Owen Williams.

facts.fact: John Robertson Architects refurbished it in 2000: the foyer was recreated largely from photographs, the façade upgraded, and the concrete frame kept.
facts.quote: As part of a redevelopment of the surrounding site the building was entirely refurbished in 2000 by John Robertson Architects. The foyer was recreated largely from photographs and the façade completely upgraded. The concrete portal frame structure was preserved.

facts.fact: Sister Express buildings were built in Manchester and Glasgow; Williams designed only the Manchester one.
facts.quote: Contrary to popular belief, the Manchester building was the only one of the three Express Buildings which Williams designed – the others in Glasgow and London were designed by Ellis and Clark.

facts.fact: Wollaton Hall is an Elizabethan country house of the 1580s on a hill in Wollaton Park, Nottingham, now the city's Natural History Museum.
facts.quote: Wollaton Hall is an Elizabethan country house of the 1580s standing on a small but prominent hill in Wollaton Park, Nottingham, England. The house is now Nottingham Natural History Museum, with Nottingham Industrial Museum in the outbuildings.

facts.fact: It was built between 1580 and 1588 for Sir Francis Willoughby and is believed to be by Robert Smythson.
facts.quote: Wollaton Hall was built between 1580 and 1588 for Sir Francis Willoughby and is believed to be designed by the Elizabethan architect, Robert Smythson, who had by then completed Longleat, and was to go on to design Hardwick Hall.

facts.fact: It is a classic prodigy house, called 'the architectural sensation of its age'.
facts.quote: Wollaton is a classic prodigy house, "the architectural sensation of its age", though its builder was not a leading courtier and its construction stretched the resources he mainly obtained from coalmining; the original family home was at the bottom of the hill.

facts.fact: A central block holds a hall three storeys high, with a 'Prospect Room' above.
facts.quote: The building consists of a central block dominated by a hall three storeys high, with a stone screen at one end and galleries at either end, with the "Prospect Room" above that.

facts.fact: Each corner has a three-storey square pavilion with decoration rising above the roofline.
facts.quote: At each corner of the house is a square pavilion of three storeys, with decorative features rising above the roof line.

facts.fact: The plan is said to derive from Serlio's drawing of the Villa Poggio Reale near Naples, with elevations from Hans Vredeman de Vries.
facts.quote: The floor plan has been said to derive from Serlio's drawing (in Book III of his Five Books of Architecture) of Giuliano da Majano's Villa Poggio Reale near Naples of the late 15th century, with elevations derived from Hans Vredeman de Vries.

facts.fact: It is built of Ancaster stone from Lincolnshire, said to have been paid for with coal from Willoughby's pits.
facts.quote: The building is of Ancaster stone from Lincolnshire, and is said to have been paid for with coal from the Wollaton pits owned by Willoughby; the labourers were also paid this way.

facts.fact: The outside and hall carry dense carved decoration, with strapwork and many decorative forms.
facts.quote: The exterior and hall have extensive and busy carved decoration, featuring strapwork and a profusion of decorative forms.

facts.fact: The Bridgewater Hall is a concert venue in central Manchester, home of the Hallé Orchestra.
facts.quote: The Bridgewater Hall is a concert venue in Manchester city centre, England. It cost around £42 million to build in the 1990s, and hosts over 250 performances a year. It is home to the 165-year-old Hallé Orchestra as well as to the Hallé Choir and Hallé Youth Orchestra and it serves as the main concert venue for the BBC Philharmonic.

facts.fact: RHWL's proposal was chosen in a design competition.
facts.quote: A competition inviting architects to present designs for the new concert hall was launched and a proposal by Renton Howard Wood Levin (RHWL) architects was chosen.

facts.fact: It held its first concert on 11 September 1996 and was officially opened on 4 December by Queen Elizabeth II.
facts.quote: The Bridgewater Hall held its first concert on 11 September 1996 and was officially opened on 4 December by Queen Elizabeth II and the Duke of Edinburgh.

facts.fact: Its 26,500-tonne superstructure rests on 280 isolation bearings of steel springs between concrete piers, insulating it from road and tram noise; it was the first concert hall built this way.
facts.quote: The main auditorium sits on a foundation of earthquake-proof isolation bearings that insulate it from noise and vibration from the adjacent road and Metrolink line. The hall's 26,500 tonne superstructure rests on 280 GERB isolation bearings consisting of rows of steel springs between concrete piers. The Bridgewater Hall is the first concert hall built with this technology.

facts.fact: Rob Harris of Arup Acoustics designed the acoustics with the hall's resident musicians.
facts.quote: The acoustics were designed by Rob Harris of Arup Acoustics in close consultation with the hall's intended musician residents.

facts.fact: The structure is mostly solid reinforced concrete, even the ceiling.
facts.quote: The structure is mostly formed from solid, reinforced concrete, "moulded and cast like a vast sculpture" — even the ceiling is concrete.

facts.fact: The lower part is deep red sandstone from Scotland, and the upper walls are clad in aluminium and glass.
facts.quote: The lower part of the hall is built of deep red sandstone from Corsehill Quarry in Annan, Scotland; its upper walls are clad in aluminium and glass.

facts.fact: It won the RIBA North West award in 1996 and the Civic Trust Special Award in 1998.
facts.quote: In November 1996, only months after opening, the concert hall won the RIBA North West award. In 1998 the hall won the Civic Trust Special Award, which is given to a building which enhanced the appearance of a city centre.

facts.fact: Bradfield Hall is an academic building on Cornell University's central campus in Ithaca, New York.
facts.quote: Bradfield Hall is an academic structure situated on central campus of Cornell University in Ithaca, New York.

facts.fact: It stands on the eastern edge of the Agricultural Quadrangle on Tower Road.
facts.quote: It is located on the eastern boundary of the Agricultural Quadrangle on Tower Road.

facts.fact: Ulrich Franzen designed it in the Brutalist style, and it was completed in 1969.
facts.quote: Designed in the brutalist style by Ulrich Franzen, the building was completed in 1969.

facts.fact: It houses departments including Crop and Soil Science and Earth and Atmospheric Sciences.
facts.quote: Bradfield currently houses Cornell's departments of Crop and Soil Science, Earth and Atmospheric Sciences, Plant Breeding and Genetics.

facts.fact: Because most laboratories are climate controlled, no rooms on the first ten floors have windows; only the hallway ends do.
facts.quote: As most of the laboratories in the building are climate controlled, none of the rooms in the first ten stories in Bradfield have windows (the hallways have windows at each end).

facts.fact: The eleventh floor houses the Northeast Regional Climate Center.
facts.quote: The eleventh floor contains the Northeast Regional Climate Center, one of the six National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration regional climate centers.

facts.fact: Franzen was a German-born American architect known for 'fortresslike' Brutalist buildings.
facts.quote: Ulrich Joseph Franzen (January 15, 1921 – October 6, 2012) was a German-born American architect known for his "fortresslike" buildings and Brutalist style.

facts.fact: The Alfonse M. D'Amato United States Courthouse is a federal courthouse in Central Islip on Long Island, New York.
facts.quote: The Alfonse M. D'Amato United States Courthouse is a federal courthouse for the United States District Court for the Eastern District of New York. It is located at 100 Federal Plaza in Central Islip on Long Island in New York.

facts.fact: Richard Meier designed the courthouse.
facts.quote: The courthouse was designed by Richard Meier.

facts.fact: It opened in 2000 and is the third largest federal courthouse in the United States.
facts.quote: It opened in 2000 and is the third largest federal courthouse in the United States (after the Thomas F. Eagleton United States Courthouse and Daniel Patrick Moynihan United States Courthouse) and the 3rd tallest and 2nd biggest building overall on Long Island outside of New York City.

facts.fact: The 12-storey building holds 23 courtrooms, 24 judges' chambers and a law library.
facts.quote: The 12-story building contains 870,000 square feet (81,000 m2), 23 courtrooms and 24 judge's chambers, as well as a law library.

facts.fact: The main entrance is through its signature conical drum.
facts.quote: Its main entrance is via its signature conical drum.

facts.fact: Courtrooms have two-storey ceilings, and upper hallways look out over the Great South Bay, Fire Island and the Atlantic.
facts.quote: Courtrooms have two-story high ceilings, and the upper floor hallways have expansive views of the Great South Bay, Fire Island and the Atlantic Ocean.

facts.fact: It stands on the grounds of the former Central Islip Psychiatric Center, closed in 1996.
facts.quote: The courthouse is one of the buildings constructed on the grounds of the former 788-acre (3.19 km2) Central Islip Psychiatric Center, which was decommissioned in 1996 after its last remaining patients were relocated.

facts.fact: The Allegheny County Courthouse in downtown Pittsburgh forms a complex with the old county jail, designed by H. H. Richardson, and counts among the finest Romanesque Revival buildings.
facts.quote: The Allegheny County Courthouse in Downtown Pittsburgh, is part of a complex (along with the old Allegheny County Jail) designed by H. H. Richardson. The buildings are considered among the finest examples of the Romanesque Revival style for which Richardson is well known.

facts.fact: Completed in 1888 and a National Historic Landmark since 1976, it was what Richardson called his 'great achievement'.
facts.quote: The current building, completed in 1888, was designated a National Historic Landmark in 1976. Richardson later referred to it as his "great achievement".

facts.fact: Richardson won a design competition, and construction began in 1884.
facts.quote: The winner of the competition was Boston architect Henry Hobson Richardson and construction of the buildings was begun by the Norcross Brothers, Richardson's construction firm of choice, in 1884.

facts.fact: Built around an interior courtyard, it lets natural light and fresh air reach most of the building.
facts.quote: The design of the main building, which Richardson considered to be his finest, was innovative in that the building is built around an interior courtyard, thus allowing natural light and fresh air to reach most of the building.

facts.fact: A 'Bridge of Sighs', based on the one in Venice, links the courthouse to the jail.
facts.quote: A prison is connected to the courthouse via the "Bridge of Sighs". The design was based on the Bridge of Sighs in Venice.

facts.fact: The whole complex is built of large rusticated granite blocks with wide arches over doors and windows, giving a heavy, dignified look.
facts.quote: The entire complex was built of large rusticated blocks of granite, with the entrance ways and windows topped with wide arches. This gives the building a heavy, stable and dignified appearance.

facts.fact: When the street was lowered in the 1900s, buried masonry was revealed and the ceremonial entrance was left a full storey above the street.
facts.quote: In the 1900s the street level in front of the building was lowered as part of a general re-grading of Pittsburgh. Richardson had anticipated this and courses of finished masonry had been buried underground, now to be revealed. This left the ceremonial entrance a full story above the street.

facts.fact: A 2007 survey for the American Institute of Architects ranked it 35th overall, above every US courthouse except the Supreme Court Building.
facts.quote: In 2007, the American Institute of Architects asked Harris Interactive to survey 2,000 people, who were shown 247 photographs of buildings and other structures in different categories chosen by 2,500 architects. The Allegheny County Courthouse was ranked 35th overall on the list and above every other courthouse in the nation except the United States Supreme Court Building.

facts.fact: Billings Memorial Library is an academic library of the University of Vermont in Burlington.
facts.quote: Billings Memorial Library is an academic library of the University of Vermont, located in Burlington, Vermont.

facts.fact: Built in 1883, it was designed by Henry Hobson Richardson to resemble his Winn Library in Woburn, Massachusetts.
facts.quote: Built in 1883, it was designed by American architect Henry Hobson Richardson to resemble the Winn Library in Woburn, Massachusetts.

facts.fact: Frederick H. Billings of Woodstock donated the library to the university.
facts.quote: The library was donated to the University of Vermont by Frederick H. Billings, of Woodstock.

facts.fact: It has been central to campus life since opening in 1885 and still looks much as it did originally.
facts.quote: It has been a central part of campus life since opening in 1885, and despite the University's growth over the intervening century, it has remained architecturally similar to its original appearance.

facts.fact: After a new library was built in 1961, Billings became a student centre in 1963.
facts.quote: A new library, the Guy W. Bailey Library (now known as the Howe Library), was built by the university in 1961 due to a lack of space at Billings Library. The Billings Library was then converted to a student center in 1963.

facts.fact: An $11.4 million renovation finished in 2018 brought academic departments back into what is called UVM's most architecturally significant building.
facts.quote: Thanks to an $11.4 million renovation completed in the summer of 2018, UVM's most architecturally significant building once again houses academic departments, including Special Collections, the Miller Center for Holocaust Studies, the Humanities Center, and the Center for Research on Vermont.

facts.fact: The Cultural Education Center stands on the south side of the Empire State Plaza in Albany, New York.
facts.quote: The Cultural Education Center is on the south side of the Empire State Plaza in Albany, New York.

facts.fact: On Madison Avenue, it faces north towards the New York State Capitol.
facts.quote: Located on Madison Avenue, it faces northward towards the New York State Capitol building.

facts.fact: Designed in the New Formalist style, it was completed in 1978.
facts.quote: Construction of the building, which was designed in the New Formalist style, was completed in 1978.

facts.fact: The eleven-storey building houses the New York State Museum, Archives and Library.
facts.quote: The eleven story, 1.5 million square foot (135,000 m³) building houses the main offices of the New York State Office of Cultural Education (part of the New York State Education Department), which include the New York State Museum (floors 1-4), the New York State Archives (floor 9), and the New York State Library (floors 5-8 and 11).

facts.fact: The Main Library is the central public library of Albuquerque, New Mexico.
facts.quote: The Main Library is a public library in Downtown Albuquerque, New Mexico and the main branch of the Albuquerque Bernalillo County Library system.

facts.fact: It opened in 1975, was designed by local architect George Pearl, and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2019.
facts.quote: Opened in 1975, it was designed by local architect George Pearl and listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2019.

facts.fact: It is a concrete-framed Brutalist building planned for a flexible interior, with a modular layout and movable partitions.
facts.quote: The library is a concrete-framed Brutalist structure designed to maximize the flexibility of the interior space with a modular layout and movable partitions.

facts.fact: Pearl counted it among his 'three or four most important' designs.
facts.quote: Pearl considered it one of his "three or four most important" designs.

facts.fact: It is Brutalist but also draws on the traditional adobe architecture of the Southwest.
facts.quote: Stylistically, it fits into the Brutalist movement, which emphasizes bold, monumental forms and raw surfaces, while also drawing inspiration from the traditional adobe architecture of the Southwest.

facts.fact: Brown brick clads the outside, with cantilevered projections on the upper floor shading large ground-floor windows.
facts.quote: The exterior walls are clad in brown brick, with a series of cantilevered projections on the upper floor. Large windows on the ground floor, protected from direct sunlight by the overhangs above, allow the building to engage passersby at street level, while glass is used only sparingly on the upper level.

facts.fact: Fixed elements such as plant, toilets and stairs sit in wings around the edge, leaving each floor open between columns 36 feet apart.
facts.quote: All fixed elements, like heating and cooling equipment, restrooms, and stairwells, were segregated in projecting wings around the periphery of the building, while the main rectangular volume of each floor was completely open except for concrete structural columns spaced 36 feet (11 m) on center.

facts.fact: Floors are divided into 9-foot-square modules, each with its own services, so sliding partitions can subdivide them freely.
facts.quote: The space is divided into 9-foot (2.7 m)-square modules, each with its own lighting, ventilation, and electrical, telephone, and video connections, allowing each floor to be freely subdivided using sliding partitions.

facts.fact: The Centre Block is the main building of Canada's Parliament on Parliament Hill in Ottawa, holding the House of Commons and Senate chambers.
facts.quote: The Centre Block (French: Édifice du Centre) is the main building of the Canadian Parliament buildings on Parliament Hill, in Ottawa, Ontario, containing the House of Commons and Senate chambers, as well as the offices of a number of members of parliament, senators, and senior administration for both legislative houses.

facts.fact: The present Gothic Revival building is the second; the first burned in 1916, leaving only the Library of Parliament at the rear.
facts.quote: Built in the Gothic Revival style, the present Centre Block is the building's second iteration. The first was destroyed by fire in 1916; all that remains of the original building is the Library of Parliament, at the rear of the Centre Block.

facts.fact: Reconstruction began immediately, led by John A. Pearson and Jean-Omer Marchand, with a design like the original but larger and with less ornament, in the Beaux-Arts spirit of the time.
facts.quote: Reconstruction of the Centre Block began immediately, with a team of architects led by John A. Pearson and Jean-Omer Marchand overseeing a design much like the original, but expanded in size and pared down in ornament, more in keeping with the Beaux-Arts ethos of the time.

facts.fact: It is a symmetrical building, 144 m long, 75 m deep and six storeys high.
facts.quote: Designed by Jean-Omer Marchand and John A. Pearson, the Centre Block is a symmetrical structure, 144 m (472 ft) long by 75 m (246 ft) deep, and six storeys high, built in the modern Gothic Revival style.

facts.fact: The walls are faced with more than 50,000 blocks of over 24 types of stone, mostly rustic Nepean sandstone.
facts.quote: The walls are faced with more than 50,000 blocks of over 24 different types of stone, though a rustic finished Nepean sandstone is the predominant kind of masonry, with dressed stone trim around the 550 windows and other edges.

facts.fact: The roof is reinforced concrete covered with copper and dotted with dormer windows.
facts.quote: The roof is of reinforced concrete covered with copper, and dotted with dormer windows.

facts.fact: The building is arranged symmetrically around the octagonal Confederation Hall, just inside the main entrance.
facts.quote: The Centre Block is arranged symmetrically around Confederation Hall, located immediately inside the main entrance. It is an octagonal chamber, the perimeter of which is divided by limestone clustered columns into eight bays of two different sizes, themselves subdivided by dark green syenite pillars.

facts.fact: From 2018, MPs moved elsewhere for renovations lasting until 2031.
facts.quote: Then, from 2018, MPs were moved elsewhere for renovations lasting until 2031.

facts.fact: The Peace Palace is an international courthouse in The Hague, home to the International Court of Justice and the Permanent Court of Arbitration.
facts.quote: The Peace Palace (Dutch: Vredespaleis [ˈvreːdəspaːˌlɛis]; French: Palais de la Paix) is an international courthouse in The Hague, Netherlands. It houses the International Court of Justice (which is the principal judicial body of the United Nations), and the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA).

facts.fact: It officially opened on 28 August 1913 as a courthouse for the Permanent Court of Arbitration, created by the Hague Convention of 1899.
facts.quote: The palace officially opened on 28 August 1913; it was built to provide a courthouse for the PCA, a court created to end war by the Hague Convention of 1899.

facts.fact: Andrew Carnegie gave US$1.5 million to build it and endow a library of international law.
facts.quote: Andrew Dickson White, whose efforts were instrumental in creating the court, secured US$1.5 million ($50,000,000, adjusted for inflation) from Scottish-American steel magnate Andrew Carnegie to build the Peace Palace to house the court as well as to endow it with a library of international law.

facts.fact: French architect Louis M. Cordonnier's Neo-Renaissance design was chosen from 216 entries in a competition called in 1905.
facts.quote: In 1904, the newly created Foundation assumed responsibility for the competition and issued the call for proposals in 1905, which led to the selection of French architect Louis M. Cordonnier's design, set in the Neo-Renaissance style, from among 216 entries.

facts.fact: To stay within budget, the design lost towers: only one big and one small tower of the planned four were built.
facts.quote: To build within budget, Cordonnier and his Dutch associate J.A.G. van der Steur adjusted the design. The palace initially had two big bell towers in front and two small ones in the back. Only one big tower and one small tower remained in the final building.

facts.fact: Thomas Hayton Mawson won a 1908 competition to design the grounds.
facts.quote: In 1908, Thomas Hayton Mawson won a competition to design the grounds.

facts.fact: The palace is filled with gifts from the member countries of the Permanent Court of Arbitration, as signs of support for its mission.
facts.quote: As a result, the palace is filled with many gifts of the Contracting Parties of the Permanent Court of Arbitration as a sign of their support for the Court's mission.

facts.fact: It received the European Heritage Label on 8 April 2014.
facts.quote: The European Heritage Label was awarded to the Peace Palace on 8 April 2014.

facts.fact: The Scheepvaarthuis (Shipping House) near Amsterdam harbour is one of the top 100 Dutch heritage sites and generally seen as the first true Amsterdam School building.
facts.quote: The Shipping House (Dutch: Scheepvaarthuis) is a building on the western tip of the Waalseiland near Amsterdam harbour that is one of the top 100 Dutch heritage sites and generally regarded as the first true example of the Amsterdam School, a style characterised by "expressive dynamism, lavish ornamentation and colourful embellishments".

facts.fact: It was built for six leading Amsterdam shipping companies, as a large cooperative office building.
facts.quote: That same year brought the commission for the Scheepvaarthuis, a large cooperative building for six Dutch shipping companies.

facts.fact: The first part was built in 1913–1916, during the First World War, and the second in 1926–1928.
facts.quote: The first part was built 1913 - 1916 (during World War I); the second part was built 1926 -1928.

facts.fact: Johan van der Mey did the architectural design, with Michel de Klerk and Piet Kramer, while the van Gendt brothers designed the concrete frame.
facts.quote: The van Gendt brothers were responsible for the technical implementation and the design of the concrete frame. The architectural design was left to the then relatively unknown architect Johan van der Mey. The Amsterdam School architects Michel de Klerk and Piet Kramer also contributed.

facts.fact: Meant as a practical modern office, it also refers to the Netherlands' maritime tradition through many maritime symbols.
facts.quote: As it was intended to serve as a practical, modern and functional office and also refer to the rich maritime tradition of the Netherlands, there are numerous maritime symbols incorporated into the design.

facts.fact: The outside is covered in carving and relief sculpture reflecting the Dutch colonial empire.
facts.quote: For example, the outside of the building is covered in carving and relief sculptures that reflect the Dutch colonial empire, with the sculpted personifications of the oceans around the main entrance presented as "exotic mysterious women".

facts.fact: To avoid colour differences, the bricks for both building phases were fired at the same time.
facts.quote: In order to avoid colour variation, the bricks were baked at the same time for both construction phases.

facts.fact: The stairwell is enclosed by stained glass by the glazier William Bogtman.
facts.quote: The stairwell is enclosed by stained-glass, implemented and designed - as was almost all the other stained-glass work in the building - by the glazier William Bogtman.

facts.fact: It became a national monument (Rijksmonument) in 1972 and opened as a hotel in 2007.
facts.quote: 1972 The Shipping House listed as a national monument (Rijksmonument).

facts.fact: Manila City Hall is the seat of Manila's city government, where the mayor holds office and the City Council meets.
facts.quote: The Manila City Hall (Filipino: Bulwagan ng Lungsod ng Maynila) is the official seat of government of the City of Manila, located in the historic center of Ermita, Manila. It is where the Mayor of Manila holds office and the chambers of the Manila City Council is located.

facts.fact: It was first meant to be part of a national government centre envisioned by Daniel Burnham in the 1900s.
facts.quote: It was originally intended to be a part of a national government center envisioned by Daniel H. Burnham in the 1900s.

facts.fact: Antonio Manalac Toledo designed it in a Neoclassical style.
facts.quote: Antonio Manalac Toledo was the architect responsible for the design of the current Manila City Hall which exhibits a Neoclassical style.

facts.fact: Toledo replaced Juan Arellano, whose Art Deco design was meant to be used before he quit the project.
facts.quote: Juan M. Arellano's design, which had an Art Deco style, was supposed to be used for the city hall but Juan Arellano quit the project and was replaced by Antonio Manalac Toledo.

facts.fact: Finished in 1941, it was heavily damaged by bombardment during the Battle of Manila in 1945.
facts.quote: Finished in 1941 right before World War II, it was another of the structural casualties of the War, heavily damaged (but still intact) by bombardment during the Battle and subsequent Liberation of Manila in February 1945.

facts.fact: It was rebuilt after the war but not to the original plans, gaining a fifth-floor attic and extra windows.
facts.quote: With the aid of the United States Army, Philippine Commonwealth Army and the city government, City Hall was reconstructed, though did not follow the original plans. Among the deviations were an added fifth-floor attic from the south entrance until the location of the east–west side entrances to accommodate additional offices, and additional windows in some areas which were formerly shelling damages.

facts.fact: The south entrance has a balcony of three arches on Corinthian columns, and the north side has a tall octagonal clock tower capped by a dome.
facts.quote: The south entrance has a balcony emphasized by three arches resting on Corinthian columns while the north rear has the same design treatment with the east and west sides, but has pediments all throughout and a tall, octagonal clock tower capped by a dome.

facts.fact: The National Museum of the Philippines declared it an Important Cultural Property on 27 June 2019.
facts.quote: The National Museum of the Philippines declared the Manila City Hall as an Important Cultural Property on June 27, 2019.

facts.fact: Dorton Arena is a 7,610-seat multi-purpose arena on the North Carolina State Fair grounds in Raleigh, opened in 1952.
facts.quote: J. S. Dorton Arena is a 7,610-seat multi-purpose arena located in Raleigh, North Carolina, on the grounds of the North Carolina State Fair. It opened in 1952 as State Fair Arena.

facts.fact: Maciej Nowicki of North Carolina State University designed it but was killed in a plane crash before construction.
facts.quote: The building was designed by architect Maciej Nowicki of the North Carolina State University Department of Architecture, who was killed in an airplane crash before the construction phase.

facts.fact: Local architect William Henley Deitrick saw it through to completion using Nowicki's design.
facts.quote: Local architect William Henley Dietrick supervised the completion of the arena using Nowicki's innovative design.

facts.fact: It was the first structure in the world to use a cable-supported roof.
facts.quote: Dorton Arena was the first structure in the world to use a cable-supported roof.

facts.fact: A saddle-shaped steel cable roof in tension is held up by parabolic concrete arches in compression.
facts.quote: Its design features a steel cable supported saddle-shaped roof in tension, held up by parabolic concrete arches in compression.

facts.fact: The arches cross about 26 feet above the ground and continue underground, where steel cables tie their ends; the outer walls carry almost no weight.
facts.quote: The arches cross about 26 feet above ground level and continue underground, where their ends are held together by more steel cables in tension. The outer walls of the arena support next to no weight at all.

facts.fact: It was one of only two new US buildings given a 1953 National Honor Award by the American Institute of Architects.
facts.quote: Dorton Arena was one of only two new building in the United States given a 1953 National Honor Award by the American Institute of Architects.

facts.fact: It inspired many architects and engineers, leading to a boom in lightweight structures.
facts.quote: The arena served as an inspiration to many architects and civil engineers, both at home and abroad.

facts.fact: Istanbul Airport is the larger of two international airports serving Istanbul, in the Arnavutköy district on the city's European side.
facts.quote: Istanbul Airport (IATA: IST, ICAO: LTFM) is the larger of two international airports serving Istanbul, Turkey. It is located in the Arnavutköy district on the European side of the city.

facts.fact: It is Turkey's largest airport and one of the busiest in Europe.
facts.quote: It is the largest airport in Turkey, the largest privately-owned airport operation in the world, and one of the busiest airports in Europe.

facts.fact: It was built far from the city because Atatürk Airport, hemmed in by city and sea, could not expand.
facts.quote: As Atatürk Airport was hemmed in by the city on three sides and the sea of Marmara on another, it was unable to expand to meet the growing demands placed on it. Sabiha Gökçen was also at capacity. The decision was taken to build a new airport, well away from the city to ensure ample space.

facts.fact: Grimshaw Architects, Nordic Office of Architecture and Haptic Architects made the concept design.
facts.quote: The architects behind the concept design were Grimshaw Architects, Nordic Office of Architecture and Haptic Architects.

facts.fact: Scott Brownrigg was the lead delivery architect and led the interior concept design with IGA Design.
facts.quote: The lead delivery architect was Scott Brownrigg, also in charge of the interior concept design with IGA Design.

facts.fact: It was inaugurated on 29 October 2018.
facts.quote: The inauguration of the airport took place on the planned date of 29 October 2018.

facts.fact: The control tower takes the shape of the tulip, Turkey's national flower.
facts.quote: The control tower is in the shape of the Turkish national flower, the tulip.

facts.fact: The first-stage main terminal covers 1,440,000 m2, the world's third-largest airport terminal building.
facts.quote: The first stage consists of the main terminal, with an annual passenger capacity of 90 million and an area of 1,440,000 m2 (15,500,000 sq ft) — making it the world's third-largest airport terminal building.

facts.fact: The Istanbul Grand Post Office is a postal building in Sirkeci, in Istanbul's Fatih district.
facts.quote: The Istanbul Grand Post Office (Turkish: Büyük Postane), or Istanbul Main Post Office, is an office building for postal services located in the Sirkeci neighborhood of the Eminönü quarter within the Fatih district of Istanbul, Turkey.

facts.fact: Vedat Tek designed it in the First Turkish National architectural style, and it was built between 1905 and 1909.
facts.quote: It was designed by architect Vedat Tek in First Turkish National architectural style and was constructed between 1905 and 1909.

facts.fact: It was first planned as the Ottoman Ministry of Post and Telegraph building and is Turkey's largest post office building.
facts.quote: It is Turkey's largest post office building.

facts.fact: It is one of the earliest examples of the First Turkish National style.
facts.quote: Architect Vedat Tek (1873–1942) designed the building as one of the earliest examples of First Turkish National architecture style.

facts.fact: The raised main entrance is reached by stairs, the building is flanked by two turrets, and the facade is cut stone and marble.
facts.quote: The main entrance is elevated reachable by stairs in front of the building. The building is flanked by two turrets. The facade is of cut stone and marble.

facts.fact: Ornament follows 16th-century classical Ottoman style, with two-colour stonework, tiled panels with geometric patterns and Kufic script, and muqarnas.
facts.quote: 16th century style classical Ottoman decorative elements are predominant in the building's ornaments including its facade with two-color stone workmanship, tiled panels with Islamic geometric patterns and Kufic calligraphic scripts, sills with tiled panels as well as muqarnas in pillar heads and corbels.

facts.fact: The main entrance opens into a three-storey atrium ringed by offices and topped by glass in mainly orange and blue.
facts.quote: The main entrance opens to a very large atrium in the center of the building. The three-story high, rectangle shaped hall is surrounded by office rooms at each floor. The atrium is topped by glass in mainly orange and blue colors.

facts.fact: Since 2000 part of the building has housed the Istanbul Postal Museum.
facts.quote: On May 6, 2000, part of the building was converted into Istanbul Postal Museum occupying four stories.

facts.fact: The Palace of Happiness is a Neo-Gothic building in central Baku, built in the early 20th century by the Polish architect Józef Płoszko.
facts.quote: The Palace of Happiness (Azerbaijani: Səadət Sarayı, Polish: Pałac Szczęścia), currently also called Palace of Marriage Registrations and previously called Mukhtarov Palace, is a historic building in the center of Baku, Azerbaijan, built in Neo-Gothic style in the early 20th century by Polish architect Józef Płoszko.

facts.fact: Oil baron Murtuza Mukhtarov had it built for his wife, Liza-Khanum Tuganova.
facts.quote: The building was built by an Azerbaijani Oil Baron Murtuza Mukhtarov for his wife Liza-Khanum Tuganova.

facts.fact: It copied a French Gothic building the couple had seen in France, and was raised in central Baku within nine months.
facts.quote: During one of their trips to France, they came across a beautiful French Gothic building. Lisa, astonished by its architecture said: "How happy the tenants of this building must be." Mukhtarov did not reply but on his return to Baku, he ordered his people off to France to purchase blue prints of the building and bring them back to Baku. An exact copy of the building was raised in central Baku within nine months.

facts.fact: It was completed in 1912.
facts.quote: On its completion in 1912, Mukhtarov surprised his wife by driving her there in a carriage and telling her that it was her new residence.

facts.fact: A statue of the Polish medieval knight Zawisza Czarny stands above the entrance.
facts.quote: An intriguing detail is the statue above the entrance of the famous Polish medieval knight Zawisza Czarny (Zawisza the Black).

facts.fact: In Soviet Azerbaijan it served as the Palace of Marriage Registrations.
facts.quote: During the existence of Azerbaijan SSR, the palace functioned as the Palace of Marriage Registrations.

facts.fact: In 2001 it was listed as a protected monument of Azerbaijani culture.
facts.quote: On 2 August 2001, by a resolution issued by the Cabinet of Ministers of Azerbaijan, the building was listed as real estate of historic and state importance and was to be protected as a monument of Azerbaijani culture.

facts.fact: It reopened on 5 July 2012 after a major overhaul and restoration.
facts.quote: On 5 July 2012 the building has been reopened after major overhaul and restoration.

facts.fact: The Lapido Building is a modernist building on 18 de Julio Avenue in central Montevideo, Uruguay.
facts.quote: Lapido Building, also known as Lapido Palace, is a modernist building in Montevideo, Uruguay, located on 18 de Julio Avenue in the city centre.

facts.fact: Juan Aubriot designed it, and it was completed in 1933 as an example of Uruguay's architectural renewal under international influence.
facts.quote: Designed by architect Juan Aubriot and completed in 1933, it is regarded as a representative example of Uruguay’s early 20th-century architectural renewal influenced by international trends.

facts.fact: It was designated a National Heritage Site in 1989.
facts.quote: The building was designated a National Heritage Site in 1989.

facts.fact: The fourteen-storey building housed the newspaper La Tribuna Popular until the 1960s.
facts.quote: The fourteen-storey building housed the headquarters of the newspaper La Tribuna Popular until the 1960s.

facts.fact: Under the 1973–1985 dictatorship, clandestine opposition publications were produced there.
facts.quote: During the civic–military dictatorship (1973–1985), clandestine opposition publications were produced there.

facts.fact: It is now used for homes and offices.
facts.quote: It is currently used as a residential and office building.

facts.fact: The Hawa Mahal is a palace in Jaipur, built of red and pink sandstone on the edge of the City Palace and extending to the women's chambers.
facts.quote: The Hawa Mahal is a palace in the city of Jaipur, Rajasthan, India. Built from red and pink sandstone, it is on the edge of the City Palace, Jaipur, and extends to the Zenana, or women's chambers.

facts.fact: Known as the 'Palace of Winds', it was built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh.
facts.quote: Hawa Mahal, also known as the "Palace of Winds", was built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh.

facts.fact: It was designed by Lal Chand Ustad.
facts.quote: It was designed by Lal Chand Ustad.

facts.fact: Its five-storey honeycomb front has 953 small jharokha windows with intricate latticework.
facts.quote: Its five-floor exterior is akin to a honeycomb with its 953 small windows called Jharokhas decorated with intricate latticework.

facts.fact: The lattices let royal women watch street life unseen, and let cool air pass through in summer.
facts.quote: The original intent of the lattice design was to allow royal ladies to observe everyday life and festivals celebrated in the street below without being seen. This architectural feature also allowed cool air from the Venturi effect to pass through, thus making the whole area more pleasant during the high temperatures in summer.

facts.fact: It is a five-storey pyramid about 50 feet (15 m) high; the top three floors are a single room wide.
facts.quote: This palace is a five-storey pyramidal shaped monument that rises to about 50 feet (15 m). The top three floors of the structure have the width of a single room, while the first and second floors have patios in front of them.

facts.fact: It fuses Hindu Rajput and Islamic Mughal architecture.
facts.quote: Its cultural and architectural heritage is a reflection of a fusion of Hindu Rajput architecture and Islamic Mughal architecture; the Rajput style is seen in the form of domed canopies, fluted pillars, lotus, and floral patterns, and the Islamic style is evident in its stone inlay filigree work and arches (as distinguished from its similarity with the Panch Mahal at Fatehpur Sikri).

facts.fact: The famous street face is actually the back of the palace.
facts.quote: Many people see the Hawa Mahal from the street view and think it is the front of the palace, but it is the back.

facts.fact: The Anna Centenary Library is a state library of the Government of Tamil Nadu at Kotturpuram, Chennai.
facts.quote: The Anna Centenary Library (ACL) is an established state library of the Government of Tamil Nadu. It is located at Kotturpuram, Chennai.

facts.fact: It is named after C. N. Annadurai, a former chief minister of Tamil Nadu.
facts.quote: It is named after a former chief minister of Tamil Nadu, C. N. Annadurai.

facts.fact: Built on 8 acres, the nine-floor library has space for 1.2 million books.
facts.quote: Built on 8 acres of land, the 9-floor library houses a total area of 333,140 sq. ft and has a capacity to accommodate 1.2 million books.

facts.fact: The library was designed by C. N. Raghavendran.
facts.quote: The library was designed by C. N. Raghavendran.

facts.fact: The building is designed so the reading area gets good daylight, with service areas on the western end to block solar radiation.
facts.quote: The building is designed in such a way that the reading area receives good daylight. The western end is flanked by the service areas to prevent solar radiation.

facts.fact: A seven-storey atrium lets in plenty of natural light.
facts.quote: The seven-storey atrium allows in abundant natural light.

facts.fact: In July 2010 it received the LEED NC Gold rating, the first library building in Asia to do so.
facts.quote: In July 2010, the library building received the LEED NC Gold rating from IGBC becoming the first library building in Asia to reach this.

facts.fact: It includes a 1,280-seat auditorium and a terrace amphitheatre for more than 800 people.
facts.quote: An auditorium of 50,000 sq. ft. with a seating capacity of 1,280, and an amphitheatre on the terrace that can accommodate more than 800 persons and two conference halls with capacities of 151 and 30 persons respectively, are some of the facilities available.

facts.fact: New Town Gate, also called Kolkata Gate, is an arch monument in New Town, Kolkata.
facts.quote: New Town Gate (also known as Kolkata Gate) is an arch-monument in the city of New Town, Kolkata, West Bengal, India.

facts.fact: It holds India's first hanging restaurant, and its visitors' gallery and restaurant are wrapped in glass with views over New Town.
facts.quote: It also houses India's first hanging restaurant. The visitors' gallery and restaurant are surrounded by glass giving a show to various parts of New Town.

facts.fact: It stands over a traffic roundabout on Biswa Bangla Sarani.
facts.quote: New Town Gate is located over the third rotary traffic island on Biswa Bangla Sarani, near Rabindra Tirtha in Action Area 1, New Town, Kolkata.

facts.fact: Construction began on 6 March 2017, and the gate opened to the public on 2 February 2019.
facts.quote: The construction of the Gate started on 6 March 2017.

facts.fact: The gate is 55 metres high.
facts.quote: This gate is 55 metres (180 feet) high.

facts.fact: A circular viewing gallery 60 metres across sits about 25 metres above the ground.
facts.quote: The 60 metres (197 feet) diameter circular viewing gallery is approximately 25 metres (82 feet) above the ground with an overall diameter of 220 metres (722 feet).

facts.fact: Two parabolic arches from the four corners of the intersection carry the ring, using about 70 tonnes of steel.
facts.quote: The ring is supported by two parabolic arches from four corners of the intersection. The four legs stand on concrete foundations 70 tonnes (70,000 kg) steel was used for the structure.

facts.fact: Two staircases and a lift reach the gallery, and up to 100 visitors are allowed on the ring at a time.
facts.quote: There are two staircases and an elevator to reach the gallery. Decorative paintings of luminaries have been drawn on the wall inside the ring with the outer side having a glass façade to have a view of the township. Maximum 100 visitors are allowed at a time on the ring.

facts.fact: Novotheatre is a planetarium on Bijoy Sarani Avenue in Tejgaon, Dhaka.
facts.quote: Novotheatre, Dhaka (formerly Bhasani Novotheatre and Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Novotheatre) is a planetarium on Bijoy Sarani Avenue of Tejgaon area in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

facts.fact: It opened to the public on 25 September 2004.
facts.quote: The Novotheatre opened to public on 25 September 2004.

facts.fact: The Ministry of Science and Communication Technology commissioned it.
facts.quote: The space center was commissioned by the Ministry of Science and Communication Technology of the Government of Bangladesh.

facts.fact: The planetarium was designed by architect Ali Imam.
facts.quote: The planetarium was designed by architect Ali Imam.

facts.fact: Built on 5.46 acres, its main space is a 21-metre dome seating 275 people.
facts.quote: Built on 5.46 acres of land, its spaces range in size from its 21-meter dome, seating 275 people;

facts.fact: The curved ceiling shows moving images of planets and stars projected onto a large dome screen.
facts.quote: The curved ceiling represents the sky and shows moving images of planets and stars through projection onto a large-screen dome at an angle of 120 degrees.

facts.fact: In 2025 it was renamed from Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Novotheatre to Novotheatre.
