facts.quote: On March 20, 2025, the interim government of Bangladesh, through an ordinance, changed the name of the Novotheater from Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Novotheatre to Novotheatre .

facts.fact: Black Star Square, also called Independence Square, is a public square in Accra, Ghana, beside the Accra Sports Stadium and the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park.
facts.quote: Black Star Square, also known as Independence Square, is a public square in Accra, Ghana, bordered by the Accra Sports Stadium and the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park.

facts.fact: It hosts the annual independence celebrations and all civic and military parades and national gatherings.
facts.quote: The square often hosts the annual independence celebrations as well as other national events, and is the site for all civic and military parades and other national gatherings.

facts.fact: Kwame Nkrumah commissioned it to celebrate Ghana's independence.
facts.quote: Kwame Nkrumah commissioned the construction of the square to celebrate the nation's independence.

facts.fact: Ghanaian architect Theo Lawson designed the square.
facts.quote: The square was designed by a renowned Ghanaian architect Theo Lawson.

facts.fact: It was completed in 1961, in time for Queen Elizabeth II's state visit.
facts.quote: It was completed in 1961, in time for the state visit of Queen Elizabeth II to Ghana.

facts.fact: Its stands seat 30,000 people.
facts.quote: In Independence Square there are stands that can seat 30,000 people.

facts.fact: Three monuments mark the fight for independence: the Independence Arch, the Liberation Day Monument and the Black Star Gate.
facts.quote: The square boasts three monuments that encapsulate the fight for independence and liberation. This includes the Independence Arch, the Liberation Day Monument, and the Black Star Gate, also known as the Black Star Monument.

facts.fact: A statue of a soldier facing the Independence Arch honours Ghanaians who died fighting for independence.
facts.quote: A statue of a soldier facing the Independence Arch symbolizes the Ghanaians who lost their lives fighting for Ghana's independence.

facts.fact: The Al-Rifa'i Mosque stands in Citadel Square, next to the Citadel, in Islamic Cairo.
facts.quote: The Al-Rifa'i Mosque (Arabic: مسجد الرفاعي, romanized: Al-Rifai, lit. 'Refaai Mosque') is a mosque located in Citadel Square, adjacent to the Citadel, in Islamic Cairo, Egypt.

facts.fact: It also serves as the royal mausoleum of Muhammad Ali's family.
facts.quote: It also serves as the royal mausoleum of Muhammad Ali's family.

facts.fact: It faces the 14th-century Mosque-Madrasa of Sultan Hassan and was conceived as a complement to it.
facts.quote: The building is located opposite the Mosque-Madrasa of Sultan Hassan, which dates from around 1361, and was architecturally conceived as a complement to the older structure as part of a vast campaign by the 19th century rulers of Egypt to both associate themselves with the perceived glory of earlier periods in Egypt's Islamic history and modernize the city.

facts.fact: The present building was built in two phases between 1869 and 1912.
facts.quote: The present structure of the Al-Rifa'i Mosque was constructed in two phases over the period between 1869 and 1912 when it was finally completed.

facts.fact: It was commissioned for Hoshiyar Qadin, mother of Khedive Isma'il Pasha, to replace an older zawiya.
facts.quote: It was originally commissioned for Hoshiyar Qadin, the mother of the 19th century Khedive Isma'il Pasha to expand and replace the old Zawiya.

facts.fact: The original architect, Hussein Fahmi Pasha, died during the first phase, and work stopped in 1880.
facts.quote: The original architect was Hussein Fahmi Pasha, a distant cousin in the dynasty founded by Muhammad Ali of Egypt in 1803, but he died during the first phase of construction, and work was halted after the abdication of Khedive Isma'il Pasha in 1880.

facts.fact: Work resumed in 1905, supervised by the Hungarian architect Max Herz.
facts.quote: Hoshiyar Qadin herself died in 1885, and work was not resumed until 1905 when the new Khedive, Abbas II of Egypt, ordered its completion. Construction work was supervised by the Hungarian architect Max Herz, head of the Committee for the Conservation of the Monuments of Cairo.

facts.fact: It was designed in the Neo-Mamluk style, then fashionable in Cairo, which referenced historic Mamluk architecture.
facts.quote: The mosque was designed in a Neo-Mamluk style, which was fashionable in Cairo at the time and which referenced historic Mamluk architecture.

facts.fact: Its two minarets rest on circular bases, like those of the Sultan Hassan Mosque.
facts.quote: The mosque has two minarets built on circular bases, like the minarets of the Sultan Hassan Mosque.

facts.fact: The Bank of China Building stands at No. 23 on the Bund in Shanghai and now houses the bank's Shanghai Branch.
facts.quote: The Bank of China Building is a tower located at No. 23 on the Bund, in Shanghai, People's Republic of China. Previously the headquarters of the Bank of China, it now houses the Shanghai Branch of the Bank of China.

facts.fact: It was built on the site of the old German Club.
facts.quote: It was built on the site of the old German Club (c. 1907).

facts.fact: In 1934 the bank's board decided to build on the former German Club site.
facts.quote: In April 1934, the board of directors decided to construct an 18-floor building, for the office administration and operation of the Head Office and the Shanghai Branch, on the former German Club site.

facts.fact: The original design had 34 floors and would have been the tallest in the Far East.
facts.quote: In the original design, this building had 34 floors and would be the highest in the Far East.

facts.fact: Victor Sassoon insisted that nothing next to his building rise above the spire of Sassoon House.
facts.quote: However, Victor Sassoon insisted that "any house built next to my building is not allowed to be higher than the spire of the Sassoon House".

facts.fact: In the end the building was cut nearly in half, topping out 1 foot lower than Sassoon House.
facts.quote: Finally, the Bank of China building was cut nearly half, with a top height 1 foot lower than the nearby Sassoon House.

facts.fact: Palmer & Turner and Lu Qianshou, the bank's chief architect, prepared the design together.
facts.quote: The design drafts were jointly prepared by a famous Shanghai design firm Palmer & Turner and Mr. Lu Qianshou (also: Luke Him Sau 1904 - 1991), the Chief Architect of the Bank of China.

facts.fact: The building was topped out in 1937, but the Second Sino-Japanese War delayed its completion.
facts.quote: The building was topped out in 1937. Right then, the Second Sino-Japanese War broke out, which postponed the completion.

facts.fact: Broadway Mansions is a nineteen-floor Art Deco building in Shanghai, now a five-star hotel.
facts.quote: The Broadway Mansions (simplified Chinese: 百老汇大厦; traditional Chinese: 百老匯大廈; pinyin: Bǎilǎohuì Dàshà, Shanghainese: Pahlowe Dusa) is a nineteen-floor Art Deco five-star hotel in Shanghai, China.

facts.fact: When completed it became Shanghai's tallest apartment building and stayed so for decades.
facts.quote: Upon its completion it became the tallest apartment building in Shanghai and remained so for several decades.

facts.fact: It stands near where Suzhou Creek meets the Huangpu River at the north end of the Bund, and its completion marked the start of Asia's high-rise era.
facts.quote: Located near the confluence of Suzhou Creek and the Huangpu River, as well as the northern end of The Bund, it was built by the architectural and engineering firm of Palmer and Turner, and its completion in 1935 heralded the commencement of the high-rise building era in Asia.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1930 and finished by October 1934.
facts.quote: Construction for the Broadway Mansions was started in 1930, and completed by October 1934, and cost $10 million (Mexican) (approximately US$3.4 million at that time).

facts.fact: It was first built in 1934 as an exclusive residential hotel, for a company controlled by Sir Victor Sassoon.
facts.quote: The Mansions was "originally built in 1934 as an exclusive residential hotel by the British". The Mansions was built by Ye Guang Estate Property Company, for the Shanghai Land Investment, Company controlled by Sir Victor Sassoon.

facts.fact: B. Flazer of Palmer & Turner designed it, and John William Barrow, of the same firm, was structural engineer.
facts.quote: The Broadway Mansions was designed by Mr. B. Flazer, and the structural engineer who supervised construction was John William Barrow, both of the architectural firm of Palmer & Turner.

facts.fact: It is a steel-framed red brick building in the stepped skyscraper mode, 78 metres tall.
facts.quote: The Broadway Mansions is a steel-framed red brick building "in the stepped skyscraper mode", that is 78 meters (256 ft) in height, with a total floor space of 24,596 square meters (264,750 sq ft).

facts.fact: Its floor plan was modelled on the Chinese character for eight, a symbol of luck and prosperity.
facts.quote: The building's floor plan was modeled after the Chinese character for the number eight, which is a symbol of luck and prosperity.

facts.fact: Dallas Hall is a historic building on the Southern Methodist University campus in University Park, Texas.
facts.quote: Dallas Hall is a historic building on the campus of Southern Methodist University (SMU) in University Park, Texas.

facts.fact: Influenced by the Roman Pantheon and Thomas Jefferson's architecture, it was built by Shepley, Rutan and Coolidge in 1915.
facts.quote: Influenced by the Roman Pantheon and architecture by Thomas Jefferson, it was constructed by the architectural firm of Shepley, Rutan and Coolidge in 1915.

facts.fact: SMU's first president, Robert Stewart Hyer, chose Georgian architecture after Jefferson's University of Virginia.
facts.quote: Robert Stewart Hyer (1860–1929), the first President of SMU, chose Georgian architecture after the Thomas Jefferson-designed architecture of the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, Virginia.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1912, and it was dedicated in 1915 as the first building on campus.
facts.quote: Construction began in 1912, and the cornerstone was laid on November 28, 1912. It was dedicated in 1915, making it the first building on campus.

facts.fact: It sits on one of the highest points in Dallas County, and it and its size gave SMU its nickname, 'The Hilltop'.
facts.quote: The site chosen for Dallas Hall is one of the highest points in Dallas County. It stood alone on a flat prairie. This, and the building's monumental size, is the origin of SMU's nickname, "The Hilltop".

facts.fact: It is a three-storey brick building.
facts.quote: Constructed of brick, it is three stories tall.

facts.fact: It was aligned so its crest lined up with the Praetorian Building, then Dallas's tallest.
facts.quote: The building was oriented so that the crest of the building perfectly aligned with the Praetorian Building, then the tallest building in Dallas.

facts.fact: A highly symmetrical campus has since grown around it, and it has been on the National Register of Historic Places since 1978.
facts.quote: A highly symmetrical campus has since been constructed around Dallas Hall. It celebrated its 100th anniversary on November 12, 2012, with a dinner for university administrators and donors. It has been listed on the National Register of Historic Places since November 17, 1978.

facts.fact: The Dr. Phillips Center is a performing arts centre in downtown Orlando, Florida.
facts.quote: Dr. Phillips Center for the Performing Arts (commonly known as Dr. Phillips Center) is a performing arts center in Downtown Orlando, Florida, United States.

facts.fact: Its grand opening was held on 6 November 2014.
facts.quote: The center's grand opening was held on November 6, 2014.

facts.fact: Barton Myers was design architect, with Artec Acoustic Consultants and Theatre Project Consultants co-designing the theatres.
facts.quote: Barton Myers was the design architect with Artec Acoustic Consultants and Theatre Project Consultants co-designing the theaters.

facts.fact: HKS Architects was executive architect, with Baker Barrios Architects.
facts.quote: HKS Architects was the executive architect in association with Baker Barrios Architects, Inc.

facts.fact: It holds the 2,700-seat Walt Disney Theater for Broadway musicals and concerts, plus the 300-seat Alexis & Jim Pugh Theater.
facts.quote: The venue features a 2,700-seat amplified hall, Walt Disney Theater, for Broadway musicals and multi-genre concerts as well as a 300-seat venue, Alexis & Pugh Theater, for smaller shows and events.

facts.fact: Steinmetz Hall, a 1,700-seat multiform theatre, can work as a concert hall, a proscenium theatre or a banquet hall.
facts.quote: Steinmetz Hall, the center’s third performance venue, is a 1,700‑seat multiform theater. It can be configured as a symphony concert hall, a proscenium theater, or a banquet hall.

facts.fact: Steinmetz Hall opened on 14 January 2022, built in a second phase.
facts.quote: Construction began on March 6, 2017, and the hall officially opened on January 14, 2022.

facts.fact: The centre occupies two city blocks.
facts.quote: The center occupies two city blocks.

facts.fact: Council House is a 13-storey office building on St Georges Terrace in Perth, for most of its history the headquarters of the City of Perth.
facts.quote: Council House is a 13-storey office building on St Georges Terrace in Perth, Western Australia.

facts.fact: The 49.8-metre building, designed by Howlett and Bailey Architects, was opened by Queen Elizabeth II in 1963.
facts.quote: Located beside Stirling Gardens and Government House in the city's central business district, the 49.8-metre (163 ft) building was designed by Howlett and Bailey Architects and opened by Queen Elizabeth II in 1963, after Perth hosted the 1962 British Empire and Commonwealth Games.

facts.fact: A jury including Harry Seidler called the Howlett-Bailey plan 'a remarkably simple solution to a complex problem' and named them competition winners.
facts.quote: The jury assessing the competition entries, which included architect Harry Seidler, described the Howlett-Bailey plan as "a remarkably simple solution to a complex problem" and declared them winners of the competition.

facts.fact: It was the first building in Perth with complete window walling, using internal blinds and external sun-breakers to cut heat gain.
facts.quote: It was the first building in Perth to use complete window walling. In order to reduce the heat entering the building through these full-height windows, the building used internal blinds and external sun-breakers.

facts.fact: T-shaped white sun-breakers coated in fine mosaic tiles alternate across the glass exterior.
facts.quote: The glass exterior of the building has T-shaped white sunbreakers superimposed in an alternating pattern across the building, coated with fine mosaic tiles.

facts.fact: In the 1990s the state government refused to heritage-list it and recommended demolition, but the City of Perth renovated it instead.
facts.quote: These conflicting views led to animosity in the 1990s, when the State Government refused to heritage list the property, and instead recommended its demolition. Despite this, the City of Perth opted to renovate the tower and keep it as its headquarters.

facts.fact: In November 2006 the Heritage Council of Western Australia recommended that it be heritage listed.
facts.quote: The Heritage Council of Western Australia recommended on 17 November 2006 that the listing of the building go ahead.

facts.fact: It has been called the most important example of modernist architecture in Perth.
facts.quote: The building, which was the favourite creation of its designer Jeffrey Howlett, has been called the most important example of modernist architecture in Perth and "one of the State's modernist icons".

facts.fact: The Bauhaus Museum Weimar is a museum of the Bauhaus design movement in Weimar, Germany.
facts.quote: The Bauhaus Museum Weimar is a museum dedicated to the Bauhaus design movement located in Weimar, Germany.

facts.fact: It shows the Weimar collections of the State Bauhaus, founded in the town in 1919.
facts.quote: It presents the Weimar collections of the State Bauhaus, which was founded in the town in 1919.

facts.fact: A project of the Klassik Stiftung Weimar, it stands near the Weimarhallenpark.
facts.quote: The museum is a project of the Klassik Stiftung Weimar and is located near the Weimarhallenpark.

facts.fact: First opened in 1995, the museum has been in a new building since April 2019.
facts.quote: Originally opened in 1995, it is now housed in a new building since April 2019.

facts.fact: The Weimarhallenpark site was chosen in April 2010 after all potential downtown sites were assessed, because the museum would shape future urban planning.
facts.quote: Because the new Bauhaus Museum was going to have a strong impact on future urban planning decisions, all the potential sites for the museum in downtown Weimar were carefully assessed before the review board selected the Weimarhallenpark in April 2010.

facts.fact: The open international design competition drew 2,189 registered architects from 60 countries.
facts.quote: A total of 2,189 architects from 60 countries registered to participate in the open international competition.

facts.fact: Heike Hanada with Benedict Tonon won one of two third prizes and were eventually appointed principal architects.
facts.quote: The two third-place prizes went to Heike Hanada with Benedict Tonon (Berlin), who were eventually appointed as principal architects, and Bube/Daniela Bergmann (Rotterdam).

facts.fact: About 14.5 million euros was allocated to constructing the museum.
facts.quote: A total of 14.5 million euros has been allocated to covering the cost of constructing the museum.

facts.fact: After Aalto's death in 1976, his office, led by his widow Elissa, completed designed works including the Jyväskylä City Theatre.
facts.quote: Following Aalto's death in 1976, his office continued to operate under the direction of his widow Elissa, who oversaw the completion of works already designed (to some extent), among them the Jyväskylä City Theatre and Essen opera house.

facts.fact: The Jyväskylä City Theatre, designed by Alvar Aalto, is the biggest theatre in the city.
facts.quote: The biggest theater in the city is the Jyväskylä City Theatre, designed by Alvar Aalto.

facts.fact: The Brooklyn Museum is an art museum in Brooklyn; at 560,000 square feet it is New York City's second largest.
facts.quote: The Brooklyn Museum is an art museum in the New York City borough of Brooklyn. At 560,000 square feet (52,000 m2), the museum is New York City's second largest and contains an art collection with around 500,000 objects.

facts.fact: Its Beaux-Arts building was designed by McKim, Mead & White.
facts.quote: Located near the Prospect Heights, Crown Heights, Flatbush, and Park Slope neighborhoods of Brooklyn, the museum's Beaux-Arts building was designed by McKim, Mead & White.

facts.fact: McKim, Mead & White won the building contract through an architectural design competition.
facts.quote: Brooklyn officials hosted an architectural design competition for the building, eventually awarding the contract to McKim, Mead & White.

facts.fact: It formally opened on 2 October 1897.
facts.quote: The Brooklyn Institute's museum formally opened on October 2, 1897, and was one of the last major structures built in the city of Brooklyn before the formation of the City of Greater New York in 1898.

facts.fact: It is a steel-frame building clad in masonry, designed in the neoclassical style.
facts.quote: The Brooklyn Museum building is a steel frame structure clad in masonry, designed in the neoclassical style by the architectural firm of McKim, Mead, and White and built by the Carlin Construction Company.

facts.fact: The original design was four times the size of what was built between 1893 and 1927.
facts.quote: The original design for the Brooklyn Museum proposed a structure four times as large as what was built from 1893 through 1927, when construction ended.

facts.fact: The 510-foot north facade has two wings flanking a projecting pavilion with a portico.
facts.quote: The primary elevation of the facade, facing north along Eastern Parkway, is 510 feet (160 m) wide and consists of the west and east wings, which flank a projecting pavilion with a portico.

facts.fact: The central portico has six Ionic columns carrying a pediment with sculptures by Daniel Chester French.
facts.quote: The center portico contains six Ionic columns that support a pediment with sculptures in its tympanum. The portico was originally accessed by a staircase that was removed in 1936–1937. Daniel Chester French was responsible for the pediment sculptures.

facts.fact: A glass entrance pavilion with four metal pylons was added in James Polshek's 2004 renovation.
facts.quote: The modern main entrance, dating to Polshek's 2004 renovation, consists of a glass pavilion with four metal pylons, as well as a semicircular plaza just outside.

facts.fact: The original building is a New York City landmark and has been on the National Register of Historic Places since 1978.
facts.quote: The original museum building is a New York City designated landmark and was added to the National Register of Historic Places in June 1978.

facts.fact: The Akita Museum of Art is an art museum in the city of Akita, Japan.
facts.quote: Akita Museum of Art (秋田県立美術館 平野政吉コレクション, Akita Kenritsu Bijutsukan Hirano Masakichi Collection) is an art museum in the city of Akita.

facts.fact: The original prefectural museum opened in 1967, and the new museum opened on 28 September 2013.
facts.quote: The original Akita Prefectural Museum of Art was opened on May 5, 1967. The new museum was opened on September 28, 2013.

facts.fact: Its main exhibit is a collection of works by Tsuguharu Foujita.
facts.quote: The main exhibit is a collection of works by Tsuguharu Foujita from the collection of the Masakichi Hirano Art Foundation.

facts.fact: The triangular building was designed by Tadao Ando.
facts.quote: The triangular-shaped building was designed by award-winning architect Tadao Ando.

facts.fact: A free-standing staircase and a triangular skylight greet visitors as they enter.
facts.quote: Some features of the museum architecture include a free-standing staircase and a triangular skylight which greet visitors as they enter the building.

facts.fact: Glass panels on the second floor, by the shop and cafe, look out over Senshu Park, the former site of Akita Castle.
facts.quote: There are also glass panels along one side of the building on the second floor where the museum shop and cafe are, which offer views of Senshu Park (the former site of Akita Castle).

facts.fact: The Cleveland Clinic Lou Ruvo Center for Brain Health opened on 21 May 2010 in Las Vegas.
facts.quote: The Cleveland Clinic Lou Ruvo Center for Brain Health (LRCBH) opened on May 21, 2010, in Las Vegas, Nevada.

facts.fact: It is run by the Cleveland Clinic and was designed by Frank Gehry.
facts.quote: It is operated by the Cleveland Clinic and was designed by Frank Gehry.

facts.fact: It is a specialised outpatient neurological centre for research, treatment and education on brain disorders.
facts.quote: The Cleveland Clinic Lou Ruvo Center for Brain Health is a specialized outpatient neurological facility dedicated to research, clinical treatment, and education regarding various brain disorders.

facts.fact: The ceremonial groundbreaking took place on 9 February 2007.
facts.quote: The ceremonial groundbreaking of the Lou Ruvo Center for Brain Health occurred on February 9, 2007.

facts.fact: Gehry's design was called 'riotously sculptural', with opposing sections alluding to the left-brain, right-brain divide.
facts.quote: The Gehry design was described as "riotously sculptural" with opposing sections that allude to "the classic left-brain, right-brain dichotomy".

facts.fact: Others called it modern architecture unmoored from aesthetics, even 'hideously awful'.
facts.quote: Others, however, suggested that it was an example of modern architecture unmoored from aesthetics, a "city unto itself" and "hideously awful".

facts.fact: It stands on land in the city's 61-acre Symphony Park in downtown Las Vegas.
facts.quote: The center operates as an outpatient treatment and research facility in downtown Las Vegas on land deeded to Keep Memory Alive, the fund raising arm of LRCBH, by the City of Las Vegas as part of its 61 acres (25 ha) Symphony Park.

facts.fact: The roughly 65,000 sq ft centre holds 13 examination rooms, offices, a 'Museum of the Mind' and a community auditorium.
facts.quote: The center is approximately 65,000 sq ft (6,000 m2) and includes 13 examination rooms, offices for health care practitioners and researchers, a "Museum of the Mind", and a community auditorium.

facts.fact: Curve is a theatre in Leicester's cultural quarter, next to the Athena conference and banqueting centre.
facts.quote: Curve, also known as Curve Theatre, is a theatre in Leicester, England, based in the cultural quarter in Leicester City Centre. Previously, it had been called Leicester Performing Arts Centre. It is adjacent to the Leicester Athena conference and banqueting centre.

facts.fact: Rafael Viñoly designed it with scenographers ducks scéno and Charcoalblue and acousticians Kahle Acoustics, with structure by Adams Kara Taylor and services by Arup.
facts.quote: Curve Theatre was designed by the architect Rafael Viñoly in association with the scenographers ducks scéno and Charcoalblue and the acousticians Kahle Acoustics; Adams Kara Taylor engineered the structure for the project whilst the Mechaical and Electrical design, including environmental controlof the theatre and foyer, and cabling distribution for theatre equipment and lighting, were by Arup.

facts.fact: It has two auditoria, a 970-seat Theatre and a 350-seat Studio.
facts.quote: It features two auditoria, one with 970 seats (referred to as the Theatre) while a 350-seat auditorium (referred to as the Studio) provides a smaller space with its own power flying system.

facts.fact: The Theatre, Studio and stages can open up into one large space for 1,300 people.
facts.quote: The Theatre, Studio and their stages can also be opened up to create one large space with a capacity of 1,300.

facts.fact: When two 18-tonne steel walls between stage and foyer are lifted, the stage can be seen from the street.
facts.quote: When the 2 18 tonne steel walls separating the stage and the foyer are lifted, the stage is visible from street level.

facts.fact: A glass façade encloses an open-plan foyer looking onto the café, bars, backstage and across the stage.
facts.quote: The glass façade encloses an open plan foyer with views onto the café, bars, backstage area, and across the stage.

facts.fact: It opened on 11 November 2008.
facts.quote: The theatre opened on 11 November 2008 with a celebratory opening show called Lift Off.

facts.fact: The project, built by Lendlease, suffered cost increases that more than doubled the first estimates.
facts.quote: The project, which was undertaken by Lendlease, was blighted by huge cost increases that more than doubled the initial estimates.

facts.fact: 425 Park Avenue is a New York office building redeveloped by L&L Holding and GreenOak Real Estate to a design by Foster + Partners.
facts.quote: 425 Park Avenue is an office building in New York City redeveloped by L&L Holding and GreenOak Real Estate, with a design by architectural firm Foster + Partners.

facts.fact: Work began in 2016 and the building was completed in October 2022.
facts.quote: Work on the new structure began in 2016, and the building was completed in October 2022.

facts.fact: It replaced a 1957 Modernist building by Kahn & Jacobs.
facts.quote: The original 388-foot (118 m) building was designed by Kahn & Jacobs.

facts.fact: Foster + Partners won a competition against final proposals from Zaha Hadid Architects, Rogers Stirk Harbour + Partners and OMA.
facts.quote: L&L solicited bids from 11 architectural firms. These entries were narrowed to four final proposals, from Zaha Hadid Architects, Rogers Stirk Harbour + Partners, OMA, and Foster + Partners.

facts.fact: Three concrete fins, each about 200 ft tall, give the Foster design a strong skyline presence.
facts.quote: Real estate news site YIMBY noted that, due to its three roughly 200 ft (61 m) concrete fins, the Foster plan would have "[...] the most pronounced skyline effect" compared to the other proposals.

facts.fact: The design has three tiers of very high ceilings and almost column-free floors.
facts.quote: Another key element of Foster + Partners design was the three tiers of very high ceiling and virtually column-free floor space.

facts.fact: Under the zoning rules, keeping at least 25% of the old structure allowed the new building to keep the original floor area.
facts.quote: If a redevelopment of a pre-1961 building could retain at least 25% of its original structure, the new building would be permitted to have up to the original square footage.

facts.fact: Twelve new jumbo columns were built, six at the front and six at the centre, with a new core at the rear.
facts.quote: Twelve new jumbo columns were erected, six as exterior columns at the front of the building and the other six at the center of the building. The new building core was also built at the rear to connect to every other floor that would be remained in the new building.

facts.fact: The building topped out on 4 December 2018 in a ceremony attended by Norman Foster.
facts.quote: The building topped out on December 4, 2018, in a ceremony attended by lead architect Lord Norman Foster.

facts.fact: Annunciation Greek Orthodox Church in Wauwatosa, Wisconsin, was designed by Frank Lloyd Wright in 1956 and completed in 1961.
facts.quote: Annunciation Greek Orthodox Church in Wauwatosa, Wisconsin, United States, was designed by architect Frank Lloyd Wright in 1956, and completed in 1961.

facts.fact: One of Wright's last works, it was finished after his death, and it is on the National Register of Historic Places.
facts.quote: It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The church is one of Wright's last works; construction was completed after his death.

facts.fact: The design reinterprets traditional Byzantine forms for a modern context.
facts.quote: The design is informed by traditional Byzantine architectural forms, reinterpreted by Wright to suit the modern context.

facts.fact: Its shallow scalloped dome is like that of Wright's Marin County Civic Center in California.
facts.quote: The church's shallow scalloped dome is similar to that of his Marin County Civic Center in California.

facts.fact: The floor plan is a Greek cross.
facts.quote: The floor plan itself is a Greek cross.

facts.fact: Wide arches carry the balcony, and the roof dome sits on an inverted dome, or bowl.
facts.quote: Wide arches support the upper level, or balcony. The roof dome sits atop an inverted dome, or bowl.

facts.fact: Much of the building uses gold-anodised aluminium, then a new material from Alcoa.
facts.quote: Much of the building utilizes a gold-anodized aluminum which, at the time, was a new material that Alcoa established.

facts.fact: Wright drew on the Hagia Sophia but meant the church as a reinterpretation of living forms, not a historicist tribute.
facts.quote: While Wright's design was inspired by traditional Byzantine forms and the Hagia Sophia in particular, the church was not meant as a purely historicist tribute; rather, it was an update and reinterpretation of architectural forms very much alive.

facts.fact: The Didrichsen Art Museum is an art museum in Helsinki, Finland.
facts.quote: Didrichsen Art Museum (Finnish: Didrichsenin taidemuseo, Swedish: Didrichsens konstmuseum) is an art museum in Helsinki, Finland.

facts.fact: Marie-Louise and Gunnar Didrichsen founded it and asked Viljo Revell to build its two phases, in 1958 and 1965.
facts.quote: The art museum was founded by Marie-Louise and Gunnar Didrichsen, who asked Finnish architect Viljo Revell to build the first of two phases in 1958 and again in 1965.

facts.fact: The modernist buildings follow the contours of the land and are surrounded by trees.
facts.quote: The modernist buildings are built to the contours of the land and surrounded by trees.

facts.fact: The museum is on the island of Kuusisaari.
facts.quote: The museum is located on the island of Kuusisaari.
